To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the social structure consists of a large number of interrelated strategic action fields, that each field is a relatively autonomous social world in which a few actors have more power and resources than others, that the boundaries of fields are permeable, that the dynamics of stability in fields are driven by the efforts of powerful actors to maintain their position, and that the dynamics of change in fields are driven in part by the efforts of less powerful actors to change their position.

(1) social structures consist of interlocking strategic action fields, (2) strategic action fields are composed of actors and the resources they control, (3) actors and resources are linked by social relations, (4) actors are motivated to pursue their interests in SAFs through the strategic use of resources, and (5) the strategic action of actors is constrained by the resources they control.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how social actors create and maintain social structures.

the ways in which the social construction of reality and the social construction of the self are interwoven in everyday life, and how this interweaving affects the way we experience our lives and our social worlds.
the relationship between the individual and the society, or, more specifically, the individual and the group.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
social movements are not only a form of social action, they are a way of seeing social action.
a general theory of action fields is a theory about the nature of the relationship between structure and agency.
the theory of strategic action field is a general theory of social structure and action.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the social world can best be conceived as an emergent, dynamic system of strategic action fields, which are themselves nested within larger systems of fields.
the SAF is a social space of strategic action in which actors engage in a process of competitive, interdependent, and bounded struggle over identities and resources.
we have a new theory for the sociology of social movements and organizations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the theory of strategic action ﬁelds provides a way to understand social structure as the emergent product of strategic action, rather than as a set of constraints on action.
the social world is composed of a large number of SAFs, each with its own unique set of rules, resources, and actors.
the social world is not made up of organizations and social movements, but of strategic action fields.
